summary: This workflow reads a members CSV file, keeps only active members, renames and drops a couple of columns, then writes the result to an output CSV. It scored 2 out of 10, meaning it is a direct translation to SQL with no complex logic. All four tools are simple, low-difficulty steps with standard SQL equivalents.

key_components.description: Loads member data from a CSV file.
Filters records to keep only those with status Active, which becomes a WHERE clause.
Selects and renames the plan_type column to plan, and drops two other columns.
Writes the final filtered and selected data to an output file, equivalent to a CREATE TABLE AS or UNLOAD in Redshift.

risks.title: CSV source has no defined data types
risks.detail: A CSV file carries no column type information, so the Redshift table used to load it must have explicit column types defined; otherwise values may be loaded or interpreted incorrectly.

next_steps: Define explicit column data types for the target Redshift table before loading members.csv via COPY.
Confirm which two columns are dropped in the Select [3] step to replicate the exact column list in SQL.
Decide whether the final output should be a Redshift table (CREATE TABLE AS or INSERT INTO) or an UNLOAD to S3.
Validate the WHERE clause logic for status = Active against the source data to ensure consistent filtering.
